questions.q: In this glossary, what does "CDM" (Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation) map to from things you already know?
options: A threat intelligence feed of known-bad IP addresses
Intune device compliance or AWS Systems Manager inventory — ongoing visibility into asset/device state
The certificate authority issuing device certificates
The SIEM pipeline storing historical activity logs
questions.explain: CDM is the trust algorithm's ongoing input on asset/device state — the same role played by Intune compliance checks or AWS Systems Manager inventory.

questions.q: Which product category is described as implementing the Policy Enforcement Point role for remote and per-application access, replacing broad VPN access?
options: SIEM
PKI
ZTNA (Zero Trust Network Access)
ICAM
questions.explain: ZTNA replaces broad, all-or-nothing VPN access with per-application, policy-checked connections — implementing the PEP role rather than being a separate concept from it.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe SASE (Secure Access Service Edge) in relation to the PE/PA/PEP model?
options: A converged networking and security edge that packages ZTNA, SWG, and CASB — essentially a packaged set of PEPs delivered at the network edge
A replacement for the Policy Engine's trust algorithm
A type of identity provider used only for workforce accounts
An alternative name for the Policy Decision Point
questions.explain: SASE converges several PEP-style controls (ZTNA, SWG, CASB) into one cloud-delivered edge platform, rather than being a new idea separate from the model.

questions.q: What is micro-segmentation's effect on the PE/PA/PEP model, according to this lesson?
options: It removes the need for a Policy Enforcement Point entirely
It replaces the Policy Engine's trust algorithm with static network rules
It only applies to traffic entering the network from outside (north-south traffic)
It pushes PEP enforcement down to the level of small internal network zones, instead of one flat "inside"
questions.explain: Micro-segmentation divides a network into small, individually access-controlled zones, pushing PEP-style enforcement down internally — applying tenets 2 and 6 to east-west traffic.

questions.q: What is an "implicit trust zone," and what is Zero Trust's stated goal regarding it?
options: A region where compliance regulations don't apply; Zero Trust ignores it
Any area still reachable without a Policy Enforcement Point evaluating it; Zero Trust aims to shrink it to nothing
A backup data center; Zero Trust requires at least two of them
The on-premises network only; Zero Trust only applies to cloud resources
questions.explain: An implicit trust zone is any traffic path that moves without a PEP checking it — exactly what Zero Trust's tenets are designed to eliminate.
